newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds edge up, await auction and CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds edge up, await auction and CPI data.

text.p: Irish government bonds gained ground in calm trade on Monday as the market was lifted by a firmer tone across Europe, dealers said.
"Most of the Irish bond market's gains were made in the morning after Friday's U.S. data. We'll be mostly focusing on domestic data and U.S. indicators on Thursday," one dealer said.
By 1525 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 had risen 13p to 103.78 to yield 6.80 percent. The eight percent bond due 2006 also rose 13p to 102.85 to yield 7.44 percent.

"Trade is now sauntering along on its own momentum. Thursday sees Irish CPI inflation data for August and the central bank's Autumn bulletin released. But the figures would need to be seriously out of line to affect the market," one dealer said.
Earlier the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) said it was holding a competitive auction of 75 million punts of the 8.25 percent bond due 2015 at 1000 GMT (1100 local time) on Tuesday.
The NTMA also said it would also hold a non-competitive auction confined to primary dealers for up to 22.5 million punts of the 20-year bond.
This week also sees the release of U.S. weekly jobless claims and producer prices data on Thursday and then August consumer prices and retail sales figures on Friday.
"If the U.S. figures prove to be stronger than expected then I think we we will see a rise in U.S. rates over the short-term," one dealer said.
